title: Five police shots hit Dustyhorn, pathologist tells coroner's inquest
article: A Saskatoon man who was shot by police likely died in seconds, a forensic pathologist testified Tuesday at the coroner's inquest into the 2007 death of Dwayne Dustyhorn.

Dr. Shaun Ladham said Dustyhorn was hit by five bullets and that one tore a major artery leading to the heart. Such an injury, Ladham said, would cause a person to lose consciousness after 15 seconds.
He added that no level of medical intervention would have saved Dustyhorn's life.
Jurors at the inquest have already heard from two Saskatoon police officers who were on the scene early in the morning of Dec. 22, 2007.
The incident began with a 911 call from Loriann Worm. Shortly after she reached the emergency line, however, she hung up.

As a result, police were dispatched to a Saskatoon basement suite on the 1200 block of Cumberland Ave South., where they found Worm and Dustyhorn inside. Officers who testified at the inquest said the 38-year-old man had two kitchen knives taped to his hands.
Cst. Henry Ly told the inquest that Dustyhorn rushed at them from inside the apartment. Ly said the man was not slowed by a closed door, throwing himself against it and tearing it from its hinges.
Ly said police decided to enter the suite to rescue Worm, and as they were about to leave, Dustyhorn rushed at them a second time.
That was when the two officers fired.
Ly said it all happened very quickly, and there was no other option.
The coroner's jury may not assign any blame for the death, but it can make recommendations to prevent similar deaths.
Another officer who was there that night was asked for his ideas on that.
Cst. Grant McMillan said there should be a policy in place where the courts do not release people who are accused of domestic violence.
Dustyhorn had a history of violence and was out on bail when he was killed.
